name: Jesse Ventura
role: Governor of Minnesota (1999-2003); former professional wrestler and actor
summary: Ventura describes himself as fiscally conservative and socially liberal and as a moderate libertarian, and he is a persistent critic of the two-party system. He favors civil liberties, cannabis legalization, abortion rights and gay rights, opposes school vouchers and the Iraq War, and wants a limited government that still keeps a basic safety net.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Opposes nationalized single-provider care but says government should step in when people cannot afford care (MinnesotaCare).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Calls himself a staunch capitalist and says competition in the private sector keeps quality high and cost low, though he says medical care cannot be purely capitalist.

unions-good.rationale: Says he and his running mate are strongly pro-union and union members; criticizes union leaders for aligning with Democrats, and in 2024 criticized Hulk Hogan as anti-union after Ventura tried to unionize wrestling.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wants government to get out of business's way, but also wants watchdog regulation to keep HMOs from getting out of hand.

cut-welfare.rationale: Wants welfare to be a safety net, not a hammock, and fears dependency, but backs a government-funded safety net; evidence points both ways.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Says he would rather face terrorists than lose any freedoms and calls federal surveillance a waste of taxpayer dollars.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Says the drug war has failed like Prohibition, addiction is a health problem, wants marijuana legalized (Marijuana Manifesto) and imagines addicts getting drugs legally; says dealers who use violence deserve severe treatment.

state-harmful.rationale: Calls himself a moderate libertarian who believes government has a role in controlling antisocial behavior.

limit-guns.rationale: Says he is no advocate of gun control and opposes registration and the assault-weapons ban, but supports waiting periods, training and permit requirements; later remarks re-examining his view are paywalled.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Said prosecuting consensual crimes such as prostitution wastes resources; in 1998 he floated legalization and then said he would not support it, so evidence is mixed.

decide-locally.rationale: Warned the federal government is leaching powers from the states, wants school decisions left to state and local authorities, and prizes states experimenting.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said prisons need a happy medium between rehabilitation and punishment, while wanting treatment rather than prison for addicts.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2000 backed domestic partnerships but not the word marriage; later reaffirmed support for gay marriage and in 2012 campaigned against Minnesota's marriage ban, saying the constitution protects people. The later view is used.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says he does not support abortion personally but it should stay legal because the government cannot ban it without abusing the Constitution.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said he does not want religious people telling him about government and objects to the religious right imposing beliefs.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Says immigration is nowhere near the catastrophe the far right claims and is an integral part of who Americans are.

free-trade.rationale: Argued in 2000 that free trade creates jobs and backed China joining the WTO, but in 2008 said he had many reservations about NAFTA.

open-borders.rationale: Said he is all for keeping trade free and borders open, while also calling for a fair and sensible policy and no benefits for illegal immigrants.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said climate change is a serious threat and criticized officials who treat it as a hoax; has proposed no specific drastic measures.

one-party-rule.rationale: Opposes the two-party system and called for parties to be abolished; advocates a bigger role for independents and third parties.

war-builds-character.rationale: Says war is failure and the result of a breakdown in public policy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Said separation of church and state deters corruption in both institutions and opposed declaring Christianity the official religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Says you cannot legislate morality and objects to fundamentalists imposing their beliefs on the legal system.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Says the extreme Right focuses too much on ideology and not enough on ideas, while also saying parties need a solid ideological base.

harm-principle.rationale: Said government's proper role is limited to judging behavior harmful to people and property and that the right to swing your fist ends at your neighbor's nose.

conscription.rationale: Opposed the draft in 1999 but in 2008 said the draft should be automatically reinstated when a vote to go to war occurs; the later view is used.

school-vouchers.rationale: Said he would say no to vouchers and no to public tax support for private schools, and wanted the word voucher erased from the vocabulary.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Wants legal immigrants granted all benefits of citizens, but illegal immigrants only emergency medical care.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Wants welfare to be tied to government-supplied work and said everyone should have a job to do.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Says the US should overcome its dependence on foreign oil and fossil fuels generally.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Called the two major parties out-of-control monsters concerned only with their own agendas and pork, and attacked career politicians and good old boys.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Says government's proper role is limited to judging behavior harmful to people and property, yet backs a government-funded safety net and MinnesotaCare.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says government must ensure every person equal access to education, housing, jobs and services regardless of who they are.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Said public schools have no business using their authority to advocate religion, though private prayer should be allowed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Argues the Bill of Rights still applies when someone is labeled a terrorist and calls the Bush Justice Department memo an attack on democracy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said government should not control the content of the Internet and should have as little to do with it as possible.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Said government limiting an artist's speech would breach the First Amendment, and that you have a right to say what you want.

death-penalty.rationale: Said earlier he would put up with the death penalty until life means life, and a note on his campaign page says that as governor he came to oppose it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Says creation belongs in Sunday school, not the science class.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Says he is not crazy about a flat tax and would rather repeal the 16th Amendment and abolish income tax.

single-official-language.rationale: Argued that official English could lead to official Christianity, which he opposes; the argument is brief.

corporate-influence.rationale: Called for banning PAC contributions and limiting soft money because candidates listen to whoever pays; criticized war contractors such as Halliburton.

non-intervention.rationale: Backed Ron Paul as the only anti-war candidate, wants troops out of the Middle East and called assassinating foreign leaders despicable.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Complains of too much secrecy in government and wants the political process televised; his books rely on declassified documents and demand open investigations.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Wants to identify which services the private sector can handle better, leaving government only those it does best.

religion-illusion.rationale: Called organized religion a sham and a crutch (Playboy, 1999) and religion the root of all evil (2010), while later saying he has no problem with most religious people; he describes himself as an atheist.

socialized-care.rationale: Refused a tax subsidy for child care, saying it is parents' responsibility.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Wants election law changed to allow full participation by credible third parties and compared Trump-era politics to a rising dictatorship.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Describes himself as fiscally conservative and socially liberal and rejects both parties, wanting neither Democrats in the boardroom nor Republicans in the bedroom.

social-market-economy.rationale: Calls himself a staunch capitalist but supports a government-funded safety net and watchdog regulation of HMOs.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Reaffirmed on the Howard Stern Show support for gay people serving in the military.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Says private charities are much better than tax-funded government programs for helping people in need.

term-limits.rationale: Said government service should be temporary, with officials serving one or two terms, because career politicians shift focus to staying in office.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Says firearms are for the protection of ourselves and others and supports concealed carry for trained citizens.

second-chamber.rationale: Advocated a unicameral state legislature, arguing the state pays two groups to do the same job.

dense-cities.rationale: Advocated smart growth focused on urban renewal instead of suburban sprawl, with transit and greenways.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Opposed the Iraq War from the beginning because the US was an aggressor and occupier.

free-public-college.rationale: Says students should not be handed a free pass and should contribute significantly to tuition.

farm-price-support.rationale: Fought to remove the federal milk law that fixes dairy prices by distance from Eau Claire, calling it stupid.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Says environmental policy should find a happy medium, with people taking priority.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Called mandatory sentences awful and opposed Three Strikes, wanting judges to keep discretion.

equal-conscription.rationale: Said that if there is a draft, women should be drafted too as long as they are not sent into combat.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Proposed replacing income tax with a national consumption tax of about 15 percent (one version exempting necessities), the opposite of cutting sales taxes.

notes: Primary-source excerpts come from OnTheIssues compilations of his books (I Ain't Got Time to Bleed, 1999; Do I Stand Alone?, 2000; Don't Start the Revolution Without Me, 2008; American Conspiracies, 2010; 63 Documents, 2011) and his 1998 campaign site; full texts were not accessible. Resolutions and policy papers he formally adopted from the National Governors Association or Midwestern Governors Conference were not treated as his own positions. Views on same-sex marriage moved from domestic partnership (2000) to marriage support; on the draft from opposed (1999) to wartime draft (2008); on the death penalty from tolerating it to opposing it.
